requirements.description: Produce every person/number cell of the present eom/eart/is/sindon and preterite wæs/wǣre/wæs/wǣron indicative series.
Produce limiting relational genitives. Follow Cook's exercise target: dependent first, head noun without its own article; retain the dependent's required article.
Preserve the head's externally governed case while its own limiting dependent remains genitive; the genitive article belongs to that dependent.
Independently formed sęllan: dative recipient, accusative thing, noun/pronoun arguments. No sęndan recipient government inferred.
Bounded subject A + copula + comparative + ðonne + parallel subject B: B is nominative, with repeated copula understood. No generalized comparative-clause or genitive-standard syntax.

Ordinary attributive adjectives are weak after article/demonstrative; bare ordinary adjectives are strong. After possessives Cook permits strong and sometimes weak; no universal possessive→weak rule and no new rule for adjectives after limiting genitives.
The six agreeing possessives have complete strong morphology. Their endings agree with the possessed noun, not the possessor; personal-genitive citations retain separate records.
Beran in carry and niman in take have an accusative person/thing as their selected ordinary object.
requirements.scope_note: The new food/fish examples are declared ordinary lexical applications, not falsely attributed source quotations; no goal or source preposition is introduced.

requirements.description: Sittan, licgan and standan describe ordinary intransitive posture; a previously taught locative on+dative phrase may locate the subject.
requirements.scope_note: No causal placement, directional complement or stand-against construction is inferred.

requirements.description: Second-singular commands address one person; plural commands address two or more, without a separate dual ending. The subject can remain unexpressed in the selected direct instructions.

requirements.description: The finite modal/volitional verb carries subject agreement; its selected plain infinitive does not acquire person/number endings or tō in the taught construction.

requirements.description: Willan plus a plain infinitive expresses desire or willingness; wolde can state past desire without asserting that the desired act occurred.

requirements.description: Open gif clauses can use indicative. A contextually tentative/hypothetical request can use present subjunctive, followed by an imperative or ordinary indicative main clause. Gif itself never licenses an automatic conversion rule.

For assigned accusative-object verbs, present or preterite wesan/bēon or weorðan + past participle expresses passive. Finite auxiliary agrees with the nominative subject. Agent omitted in productive tasks; no new fram-agent rule needed. Wesan often presents state/result and weorðan event, but not an absolute contrast or one-to-one English tense mapping.
Be in the midst of a dative landmark.
requirements.scope_note: Only this selected lexical frame; no arbitrary case-government generalization.

requirements.description: Independent present subjunctive expresses wishes/exhortations, including thirdperson Let... and firstplural Letus.... Secondperson imperative and subjunctive are formally/syntactically distinct even where spellings coincide. English let here is not a new lǣtan causative construction.

Direct yes/no questions commonly begin with the finite verb; wh-words or phrases commonly precede the finite verb, and a wh-subject is itself the subject. No English dummy do is added. These are tendencies, not an exceptionless V2 transformation.
The inflected se/sēo/ðæt series can introduce relative clauses alone or followed by ðe; reuse its full NGDA morphology with newly taught relative function.

In selected productive relative clauses, gender and number track the antecedent while relative case is governed by its function within its own clause. An antecedent in dative can have a nominative relative, and vice versa; this is the selected ordinary construction, not a universal ban on attraction.
Invariant ðe introduces an ordinary relative clause and can represent different internal case functions; it is not an English personal interrogative pronoun.
Hātan command takes accusative actor + plain infinitive. The infinitive may retain its own accusative object.
requirements.scope_note: Select hātan for II.12.5; no unnecessary gebēodan system. Dative reporting addressee is a different function.

requirements.description: Sęcgan can name its recipient in the dative with direct speech or a dependent content/question complement.
Wh question clauses can be complements of witan or sęcgan, including Saga mē + wh clause. The wh form takes its internal case.
requirements.scope_note: This is an embedded question, not an ordinary relative antecedent construction. Subjunctive is a normal selected reporting/question pattern; factual indicative is defensible in suitable context.
